# Xue

> Xue (雪, "snow") is an open-source, static-site viewer of weather
> forecasts. It plays whole NOAA GFS, ECMWF IFS, ECMWF AIFS, ECMWF IFS HRES,
> NOAA HRRR, NOAA GEFS-Aerosols, NCEP CFSv2, DWD ICON-EU and Météo-France
> ARPEGE runs — 2 m temperature, precipitation rate, 10 m and upper-air wind, sea
> level pressure, isobaric geopotential height, temperature, humidity and
> water vapour flux, aerosol optical depth and particulate matter, out to
> 240 hours (360 for AIFS and IFS HRES, 18 for HRRR, 120 for
> GEFS-Aerosols and ICON-EU, 102 for ARPEGE, 6552 — thirty-nine weeks —
> for CFSv2) — as
> smooth animations over a
> MapLibre basemap, decoding per-variable Zarr v3 stores laid out for
> playback (quantized uint8, small tiles × six-frame chunks; the custom
> `.xue` container they grew out of is no longer published, since
> 2026-09-15) in a Rust/WebAssembly worker and rendering on the GPU. Live at https://xue.ringsaturn.me. Code at
> https://github.com/ringsaturn/xue (MIT OR Apache-2.0).

Facts worth getting right:

- Live sources, one shell (the ids are the `?model=` and `--model` values).
  Forecasts: `gfs`, `sflux`, `ecmwf`, `ifs`, `aifs`, `ifshres`, `hrrr`,
  `gefsaero`, `cmadust`, `silam`, `cfs`, `iconeu`, `arpege`. Observations:
  `mrms`, `jma`, `aurora` and the satellites `himawari`, `himawarijp`,
  `goeseast`, `goeswest`, `meteosat`. Cases only (no live pointer, no place
  in the model switch): `mrms3d`, `woof`, `efas`, `efaswb`, `era5`, `cams`.
  The grid, axis, cadence, variables and caveats of each are in
  [docs/sources.md](https://github.com/ringsaturn/xue/blob/main/docs/sources.md)
  (also in llms-full.txt); the satellite channels and composites (`ir104`,
  `dustrgb`, `dustcf`, `zhouye`, `truecolor`) in
  [docs/satellite.md](https://github.com/ringsaturn/xue/blob/main/docs/satellite.md).
  The intro above gives each forecast's horizon. An observation dataset has
  no run cycle and no lead time: its `run` is the hour its series starts and
  a frame's offset is time elapsed since.
- Bundles published per run. GFS and ECMWF: `tmp2m`, `prate`, `prmsl`,
  the geopotential height `hgt<level>`, temperature `tmp<level>` and
  relative humidity `rh<level>` on each of the eight isobaric surfaces
  (`<level>` one of 1000, 925, 850, 700, 500, 300, 250, 200 hPa — the
  mandatory radiosonde levels), the surface diagnostics `gust`, `tcdc` (total
  cloud cover), `cape`, `dpt2m`, the vertical velocity `vvel850`,
  `vvel700`, `vvel500`, the 850 hPa equivalent potential temperature
  `thetae850`, the clear-air turbulence `cat300`, `cat250`, `cat200` (an
  eddy dissipation rate in m^(2/3)/s: the Ellrod TI1 index of the resolved
  wind projected onto the climatological EDR distribution, no convective or
  mountain-wave turbulence), the ocean fields `tmpsfc` (surface / skin temperature, the
  SST over water), `icetk` (sea ice thickness), `htsgw` and `perpw`
  (significant wave height and primary wave period, from the wave model of
  the same cycle — GFS-Wave, ECMWF's `wave` stream; land is 0 in both), the
  soil layers `tsoil1`–`tsoil4` (soil temperature, °C) and `soilw1`–`soilw4`
  (volumetric soil water, m³/m³), layer 1 at the surface — the id is the
  layer's index and its depth is the model's: GFS 0–10, 10–40, 40–100,
  100–200 cm; ECMWF 0–7, 7–28, 28–100, 100–289 cm. Code 0 of either is
  "no soil" (−61 °C / −0.01 m³/m³, one step below any real value): open
  water on GFS, and sea ice for GFS's water content (1 over the ice
  sheets); ECMWF has no such mask
  (its sea holds the model's temperature and a water content of 0) — and
  the vector pairs `wind10m`, `wind<level>` on the same eight surfaces,
  `qflux850` and `wave` (the height laid along the direction the waves travel, u/v in
  metres — the viewer's wave layer; the primary direction is read from it
  as `atan2(-u, -v)`, degrees true the waves come from, and is not
  published as a scalar). Both also carry the model's own terrain height
  `orog` (metres) — a static bundle, one frame at the analysis and nothing
  to play. On ECMWF the gust is the maximum over the
  interval ending at the frame (ECMWF `10fg`) and, like `prate`, has no
  analysis frame; its CAPE is the most-unstable parcel's (`mucape`), its
  wave period the peak period (`pp1d`); its `orog` is the surface
  geopotential divided by g. GFS additionally: the wind sea and the first
  (strongest) swell partition from GFS-Wave — `wvhgt` / `wvper` (wind-wave
  height and mean period), `swhgt` / `swper` (swell height and mean period)
  and the vector pairs `windwave` and `swell` built the way `wave` is (their
  directions are not published as scalars) — `lcdc`, `mcdc`,
  `hcdc` (low / middle / high cloud cover), `vis`, `aptmp2m` (apparent
  temperature), `cin` (convective inhibition), `pwat` (precipitable water),
  `hpbl` (planetary boundary layer height), `ptype` (the categorical
  precipitation type derived from the model's four rain / freezing-rain /
  ice-pellet / snow flags), `cpofp` (the model's percent of the precipitation
  falling frozen) and `fzlvl` (the 0 °C isotherm's height above sea level), both
  also on HRRR, the 100 m wind pair `wind100m`, and `icec` (sea
  ice cover), which the ECMWF open data does not carry. ECMWF and IFS publish `ptypeec`, the
  model's own type. `?phase=on` paints `prate` by phase from those fields, with
  the line where `fzlvl` meets `orog` and the freezing rain zones. The `sflux` view
  reads its pressure levels, `prmsl`, `ptype`, `cpofp` and `fzlvl` from the same
  cycle's `gfs` stores. AIFS: the ECMWF set less what its open data lacks — no
  `rh850` / `rh700` / `rh500` (it carries specific humidity only), no
  `gust`, `cape`, `icetk` or `perpw`, and of the soil only the top two
  layers (`tsoil1`, `tsoil2`, `soilw1`, `soilw2`, the water content
  "no soil" over the sea) — plus `lcdc`, `mcdc`, `hcdc`; its
  `prate` is de-accumulated from a run total in millimetres and is a mean
  over the six-hour step. IFS (`ifs`): the ECMWF set as published, on the
  0.1° grid. SFLUX: `tmp2m`,
  `prate`, `dswrf`, `orog`, `wind10m`. IFS HRES (`ifshres`): the GFS surface set its
  9 km product carries — `tmp2m`, `prate`, `dswrf`, `prmsl`, `gust`,
  `tcdc`, `lcdc`, `mcdc`, `hcdc`, `cape`, `vis`, `dpt2m`, `tmpsfc`,
  `icetk` and the vector pair `wind10m`, fifteen in all; no isobaric
  levels, no waves, no sea ice cover. Its `prate` is the interval total
  divided by the step and, like `dswrf` and `gust`, has no analysis
  frame. HRRR: `tmp2m`, `prate`, `prmsl`, `hgt850`,
  `hgt700`, `hgt500`, `tmp925`, `tmp850`, `tmp500`, `gust`, `tcdc`,
  `lcdc`, `mcdc`, `hcdc`, `cape`, `vis`, `dpt2m`, the forecast composite
  radar reflectivity `cref` (the same name and unit as the radar mosaics'),
  the static terrain `orog`, and the vector pairs `wind10m`, `wind80m`,
  `wind925`, `wind850`, `wind250`.
  GEFS-AEROSOLS: `aod` (aerosol optical depth at 550 nm, total,
  dimensionless), `aoddust`, `aodsalt`, `aodsulf`, `aodorg`, `aodbc` (the
  same for dust, sea salt, sulphate, organic carbon and black carbon),
  `pm25`, `pm10` (surface PM2.5 and PM10, µg/m³) and `pm10dust` (the PM10
  of dust alone); every one a GRIB2 aerosol product whose species and
  size / wavelength intervals are the `aerosol` block beside the
  variable's `parameter` in the bundle metadata. CMA-CW-DUST (`cmadust`):
  `dustsfc` (the surface dust concentration of every particle size,
  µg/m³, to 50,000 — not `pm10dust`, which is dust under 10 µm; WMO
  0/20/0 on the ground with a dust `aerosol` block of no size interval)
  and `aoddust` (the dust optical depth at 550 nm, GEFS-Aerosols'
  identity and scale, so a storm core past 5 reads as the top of the
  scale). SILAM (`silam`): `pm25` and `pm10`, the total of every
  aerosol the model carries, on the GEFS-Aerosols identities. CFSv2 (`cfs`): on the T126
  Gaussian grid `tmp2m`, `prate`, `tcdc`, `dswrf`, `tmpsfc`, `icec`,
  `icetk` and the vector pair `wind10m`; on the 1° grid `prmsl`,
  `hgt1000` / `hgt850` / `hgt700` / `hgt500` / `hgt200`, `tmp1000` /
  `tmp850` / `tmp700` / `tmp500` / `tmp250` / `tmp200`, `vvel500`, the
  vector pairs `wind1000` / `wind925` / `wind850` / `wind700` / `wind500` /
  `wind250` / `wind200` and `qflux925` / `qflux850` / `qflux700` /
  `qflux500` — thirty-two in all, every series starting at F6 rather than
  at the analysis; its `prate`, `dswrf` and `tcdc` are means over the six
  hours ending at the frame. ICON-EU (`iconeu`) and ARPEGE (`arpege`):
  `tmp2m`, `prate`, `prmsl`, `gust`, `tcdc` and the vector pair `wind10m`,
  six each; `prate` is de-accumulated from the run total and, like `gust`
  (the maximum over the step, or the hour on ARPEGE, ending at the frame),
  has no analysis frame. CMA:
  `cref`. MRMS: `cref` (observed composite reflectivity, dBZ), `prate`
  (the MRMS precipitation rate, mm/h) and `rqi` (the radar quality index,
  0–1; code 0 is outside radar coverage, which `cref` code 0 does not tell
  from no echo); a case may ship the reflectivity alone. MRMS3D: `refl3d` (the 33-level volume above). WOOF-WRF
  (`woof`): `tmp2m`, `prate`, `tmpsfc`, `dpt2m`, `tcdc`, `lcdc`, `mcdc`,
  `hcdc`, `hpbl`, `dswrf`, the static `orog` and the vector pair
  `wind10m` — the same names and units as the GFS's, so a case ships a
  subset of them — and `cloud3d`, the cloud water volume: the mixing ratio
  (g/kg, GRIB2 0/1/22 on surface 102) on 24 altitudes above mean sea level
  (every 0.25 km from 0.25 to 3 km, every 0.5 km to 6 km, every 1 km to
  12 km; variables `clw250` … `clw12000`), 0 g/kg below the model ground. JMA: `prate` (precipitation intensity class representative rate,
  mm/h). HIMAWARI: `ir104` (10.4 µm brightness temperature, K) and
  `dustrgb` (the Dust RGB's red, green and blue guns, 0–1, a composite
  with no physical unit), `dustcf` (the DEBRA dust confidence, 0–1) and
  `zhouye` (the ZHOUYE dust confidence, 0–1, diurnally consistent) and
  `truecolor` (the true colour picture's red, green and blue guns, 0–1,
  a composite with no physical unit, infrared cloud over a dark ground
  after dark; GOES-EAST and GOES-WEST the same five, METEOSAT and
  HIMAWARI-JP `ir104`, `dustrgb` and `truecolor`). AURORA:
  `aurora` (aurora visibility probability, percent, on a 1° global grid).
  EFAS-v5 and EFAS-v5-WB (`efas`, `efaswb`): `dis06` (river discharge,
  the mean over the six hours ending at the frame, m³/s, GRIB2 1/0/7 with
  statistical process 0), `disrp` (its return-period class against the
  EFAS thresholds, producer `xue`, local 1/192/1: 0 below the 1.5-year
  level, 1 at or above it, 2 the 2-year, 3 the 5-year, 4 the 20-year) and
  `upstream` (the area draining through the cell, km², producer `xue`,
  local 1/192/2, static); all three exist only on river cells, and the
  viewer draws them cell by cell, without smoothing.
  Names
  are `<family><level>`; the level is in hPa, `2m`/`10m` are heights above
  ground, `prmsl` is mean sea level pressure.
- Only the newest run per source is kept online. Runs are pruned when
  superseded; historical events survive only as cases (below).
- The site is entirely static: Cloudflare Pages for the shell, a public R2
  bucket for data, HTTP Range requests for streaming. No account, no cookies.
- An experimental read-only JSON API (no compatibility, reliability or
  freshness guarantee) over the same public bucket is at
  https://xue-api.ringsaturn.me: `GET /v1/catalog`, `GET
  /v1/sources/{source}` (the live run and its variable list), and `GET
  /v1/point?source=&lat=&lon=&variables=` for one cell's series (ISO 8601
  `time`, or the whole axis). It never writes data, and the site does not
  depend on it.
- Licensing is in three parts: the code MIT OR Apache-2.0; the
  specifications under `docs/` CC BY 4.0; the published data under each
  source's terms (every STAC Collection names them under `license` and
  `providers`), with Xue's own contribution to each object CC BY 4.0
  (credit the source as it asks and add "via Xue").
- Data licensing: NOAA GFS, GEFS-Aerosols, HRRR and NCEP CFSv2 are public domain; ECMWF open data is CC BY 4.0 and
  what is served is a converted derivative ("Contains modified ECMWF open
  data"); `iconeu` is DWD open data under CC BY 4.0 ("Source: Deutscher
  Wetterdienst", quantized); `arpege` is Météo-France data from data.gouv.fr
  under the Licence Ouverte / Etalab 2.0 ("Source: Météo-France"); `cma` is a CMA product (中国气象局国家气象中心, www.nmc.cn) and `mrms` a
  NOAA product (public domain); `jma` is derived from the Japan Meteorological Agency
  website (出典：気象庁ホームページ; the agency's terms of use, compatible
  with CC BY 4.0, ask that the source be named and the processing —
  regridding and reclassification by jma-radar — be noted); `himawari` and
  `himawarijp` are JMA's Himawari-9 imagery distributed by NOAA
  (attribution required, the reprojection noted, no endorsement implied by
  either agency); `goeseast`
  and `goeswest` are NOAA GOES-R imagery (public domain, attribution
  requested, no endorsement implied); `meteosat` is EUMETSAT Meteosat
  data, the hourly Level 1 cycle, CC-BY-4.0 ("Contains modified EUMETSAT
  Meteosat data <year>", the year of distribution stamped where the
  attribution is shown; no endorsement implied); `aurora` is NOAA SWPC's
  OVATION model output (a US Government work, public domain, attribution
  requested, no endorsement implied); `ifshres` is ECMWF IFS HRES
  forwarded by Open-Meteo, CC BY 4.0 ("Adapted from ECMWF IFS by ECMWF,
  licensed under CC BY 4.0", via Open-Meteo, open-meteo.com — neither
  ECMWF nor Open-Meteo endorses this use); `efas` and `efaswb` are
  Copernicus Emergency Management Service information from the Early
  Warning Data Store, under its terms ("Contains modified Copernicus
  Emergency Management Service information"); `era5` is Copernicus
  Climate Change Service information from the Climate Data Store,
  CC-BY-4.0 ("Contains modified Copernicus Climate Change Service
  information"; cite Hersbach et al., doi:10.24381/cds.adbb2d47); `cams` is
  Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service information from the
  Atmosphere Data Store, CC-BY-4.0 ("Contains modified Copernicus
  Atmosphere Monitoring Service information"; doi:10.24381/04a0b097);
  `cmadust` is the China Meteorological Administration's CMA-CW v1.0/DUST
  forecast of the WMO SDS-WAS Asian Center, obtained through WMO WIS2,
  where it is exchanged as core data under the WMO Unified Data Policy
  (Resolution 1 (Cg-Ext(2021)): free and unrestricted); `silam` is the
  Finnish Meteorological Institute's SILAM forecast, CC-BY-4.0 ("Source:
  Finnish Meteorological Institute, SILAM"); the basemap
  is Protomaps © OpenStreetMap contributors.

## The geostationary mosaic

`/?model=geo` is a view, not a dataset: the shell opens the published run of
every geostationary imager that answers (Himawari-9, GOES-18, GOES-19 and,
when published, Meteosat-12), clips each layer to the longitudes it sees least
obliquely (a partition at the midpoints between sub-satellite longitudes,
since every imager sits over the equator) and follows one timeline by valid
time, the ten-minute disks driving it and an hourly member holding its frame
for the hour. Nothing is uploaded for it and no pointer names it; a disk
whose pointer is missing leaves the basemap between its neighbours' edges.

## Pages and URL parameters

The viewer is one page whose state is in the query string. Unknown values
fall back to defaults rather than fail, so a constructed link always opens.

- https://xue.ringsaturn.me/ — the live viewer. Defaults to GFS precipitation.
- https://xue.ringsaturn.me/showcase.html — the list of historical cases.
- https://xue.ringsaturn.me/tc/ — one static page per archived tropical
  cyclone of the seasons with forecasts (`/tc/<season>/<name>-<atcf id>`),
  per season (`/tc/<season>/`) and
  for the archive, in English and under `/zh/`, `/zh-hant/`, `/ja/`, `/ko/`:
  the storm's facts, its six-hourly best track, a track picture and the
  forecast track errors by source and lead, each linking to the map below.
- https://xue.ringsaturn.me/typhoon.html — past tropical cyclones on a map,
  picked by season, basin and storm in the panel beside it (`?storm=<ATCF
  id>`, e.g. `WP062023`, or a storm with no number's history id, e.g.
  `WP-1951123N10140-1951` (`WP-COBRA-1944` for a storm reconstructed from primary sources, whose record lists them under `provenance`); `?issue=YYYYMMDDHH` picks the issue time drawn;
  without a storm, the latest of the season running now): the centres' best
  tracks, every archived forecast started at that time (official,
  deterministic, ensemble), and the storm's track errors in km by source and
  lead.
- https://xue.ringsaturn.me/compare.html — every live forecast model at
  one point on one clock (`?lat=<deg>&lon=<deg>`, `?span=120|360` hours,
  `?fields=tmp2m,prate,wind10m,...` among `tmp2m dpt2m prate wind10m gust
  tcdc prmsl`), one block per model with the run in its header, a row of
  local hours and a row per field, the nearest airport's METAR reports
  (within 40 km) as a block of the same shape; values are the model's
  nearest grid cell, not interpolated. The viewer's point probe links here.
- https://xue.ringsaturn.me/metrics.html — when each forecast run went
  live, measured from the publish workflows: per source the latest run,
  latency after the cycle time (median / p90 / max), missing cycles and
  workflow outcomes over the window, and for each deadline (ERCOT
  day-ahead close, 10:00 US Central) the newest run live at the cutoff on
  each day. Measurements, not an SLA; the data is `metrics/latency.json`
  at the data root (docs/metrics.md).
- `?model=gfs|sflux|ecmwf|ifs|aifs|ifshres|hrrr|iconeu|arpege|gefsaero|cmadust|silam|cfs|mrms|jma|cma|himawari|himawarijp|goeseast|goeswest|meteosat|aurora|geo`
  — which live source (`ifs-0p1` is an alias of `ifs`, `aifs-single` of
  `aifs`, `hres` / `ifs9km` of `ifshres`, `cfsv2` of `cfs`, `icon-eu` / `icon` of `iconeu`, `cma-dust` / `cma-cw-dust` of `cmadust`, `silam-aq` of `silam`, `hrpns` of `jma`, `radar` of `cma`, `himawari-9` / `ahi` of
  `himawari`, `himawari-jp` of `himawarijp`, `goes-19` / `goes-18` of
  `goeseast` / `goeswest`, `mtg` /
  `meteosat-12` of `meteosat`, `mosaic` / `geostationary` of `geo`, the
  mosaic of every geostationary disk). `woof` (`wrf`), `efas`,
  `efaswb`, `era5` and `cams` are known but have no live run, so alone they open the
  default; a case pins its own dataset.
- `?type=` — the filled layer: `temp` (2 m temperature), `precip`, `wind`
  (10 m), `solar` (sflux only), `pressure` (sea level pressure as isobars),
  `radar` (composite reflectivity: the radar cases, and the HRRR forecast), the GFS
  and HRRR surface diagnostics `gust`, `cloud`
  (`lowcloud` / `midcloud` / `highcloud` for the layers), `cape`,
  `visibility`, `dewpoint`, `feelslike`, the GFS ocean set `sst` (the
  skin temperature, `tmpsfc`), `seaice` (`icec`; `icethickness` for
  `icetk`), `waves` (the `wave` vector — height as the fill, direction as
  particles; `waveheight` for the scalar `htsgw`, `waveperiod` for
  `perpw`), the Himawari `infrared` (`ir104`; `ir`, `satellite` and `sat`
  are accepted spellings), `shortwave` (`ir039`, the 3.9 µm window a
  burning pixel shows in, on the disks that publish it; `swir`, `ir39`),
  `dustrgb` (`dust`), `debra` (`dustcf`,
  `dustconfidence`), `zhouye` (`zhouyecf`), `truecolor` (`visible`,
  `rgb`, `color`, `colour`), the GEFS-Aerosols `aod` (`aod550`; `aoddust`,
  `aodsalt`, `aodsulf`, `aodorg`, `aodbc` by species), `pm25` (`pm2p5`),
  `pm10` and `pm10dust`, the CMA-CW-DUST `dustsfc` (`surfacedust`,
  `sanddust`, `duststorm`), the EFAS `returnperiod` (`disrp`, `floodclass`,
  `rp`), `discharge` (`dis06`, `dis`, `riverdischarge`, `streamflow`) and
  `upstream` (`upstreamarea`, `uparea`, `catchment`), or a bundle name such as `tmp850`,
  `rh700`, `wind850`, `qflux850`, `hgt500`, `vvel700`, `thetae850`; `t850`,
  `z500`, `humidity700`, `vapour850`, `omega700`, `subtropicalhigh`
  (= `hgt500`) are accepted spellings.
- `?lines=` — a contour overlay from the pressure family over any filled
  layer: `pressure` (sea level) or `hgt850|hgt700|hgt500|hgt250`.
- `?volume=cloud3d` — draw a run's volume bundle as a 3D volume over the
  2D field on screen (the cloud water of a `woof` case); ignored when the
  run does not ship it or the field is itself a volume.
- `?vexag=<number>` — the vertical exaggeration of a 3D volume, up to 200:
  by default 1 (true scale) for a volume under two degrees of longitude
  wide and 10 for a wider one. With the terrain on, the terrain's own
  exaggeration multiplies it, so the volume stays registered to the
  relief.
- `?case=<id>` — a historical case; ids come from the catalog below.
- `?res=half|full` — pin the resolution tier instead of choosing it from the
  viewport and connection.
- `?accum=<window>` — with `type=precip`, draw the precipitation total over
  the window ending at the playhead instead of the rate, summed in the
  browser from the rate frames: `3h`, `6h`, `12h`, `24h`, `48h` or `72h` on
  a forecast, `10m`, `30m`, `1h` or `3h` on a radar or nowcast window
  (each where the dataset's axis is long enough). A window the dataset does
  not offer shows the rate.
- `?particles=off` — hide the wind particle animation (default on, off under
  prefers-reduced-motion).
- `?projection=globe` — draw the map as a globe (default: the flat Web
  Mercator plane).
- `?terrain=on|<exaggeration>` — lift the ground into 3D relief with the
  forecast draped over it (`on` = 1.5×, a number up to 10). Bearing and
  pitch go in the camera fragment: `#map=<zoom>/<lat>/<lon>/<bearing>/<pitch>`.
- `?shadow=on` — cast the terrain's shadows for the sun at the frame's valid
  time (or now, before data loads), over the basemap and the forecast, flat
  or in 3D relief, from zoom 9 in (default off).
- `?contours=on` — draw elevation contour lines over the relief, cut in the
  browser from the terrain tiles (500 m at zoom 9 down to 25 m at zoom 15,
  the index line every fifth labelled in metres), from zoom 9 in (default
  off; also a switch on the view tile).
- `?lang=zh|zh-Hant|en|ja|ko|de|fr|es|pt|tr|ru` and `?theme=light|dark` —
  otherwise the browser's language and colour scheme decide.
- `?tc=<storm id>` — focus one tropical cyclone (an ATCF id such as
  `EP142026`, or the product's `x-<basin>-<hour>-<n>` id for an unnumbered
  system) and frame it; `?tc=off` hides the storm tracks; absent, every
  named system is drawn over whatever layer is on screen. `?tcagency=nhc,jtwc`
  and `?tcmodel=gfs,ecmwf` narrow the official and model tracks drawn
  (absent means all); `?tcmembers=on` adds the ensemble members.
- `?stations=snd|apt|syn|fire|aq|alerts` (comma-joined for more than one) — draw the
  station marks over whatever layer is on screen: `snd` the radiosonde
  soundings (one circle per station, filled by its 500 hPa temperature;
  the card reads the headline the index carries), `apt` the airports (one
  circle per station, coloured by its flight category; below zoom 6 only
  the stations with a current TAF), `syn` the surface weather stations
  (one small circle per station, filled by its current temperature, grey
  where it has no thermometer; principal stations at every zoom, automatic
  ones from zoom 5, precipitation gauges from zoom 7), `fire` the NASA
  FIRMS active fires of the 24 h ending at the playhead (sized by fire
  radiative power, red when recent and brown a day old, clustered at low
  zoom; `docs/fire.md`; a showcase case's own round instead keeps every
  detection up to the playhead, the newest satellite pass yellow, the one
  before red-orange, older ones a dark red stipple, with a white arrow for
  the mean 10 m wind since the newest pass), `aq` the air-quality stations
  (one circle per station on fixed PM2.5 steps in µg/m³, hollow where it
  measures no PM2.5; concentrations only, no index; `docs/aq.md`), `alerts`
  the weather warnings in force now (areas filled by the common 1–5 level,
  level 5 violet; a snapshot of the latest round, not of the playhead;
  clicking inside one lists every warning in force there;
  `docs/alerts.md`). Absent, or
  `?stations=off`, draws none — the default, since thousands of marks on a
  world view read as texture rather than data. `sounding`, `airport`,
  `synop`, `surface`, `fires`, `firms`, `airquality`, `pm25`, `alert`,
  `warnings`, their plurals, `on` and `all` are accepted
  spellings. The marks follow the playhead's valid time only in
  that a station observed far from it is drawn faint; they load nothing
  per frame and never hold up playback. Both products also answer a pinned
  point whatever this parameter says: clicking the map draws the nearest
  ascent within 150 km as a skew-T under the meteogram rows, with the run's
  own isobaric levels dotted over it, and lays the nearest airport's last
  day of METARs — and its TAF, as a row of forecast periods — over the rows
  themselves. A surface station within 20 km at about the pin's ground
  height (within 300 m) takes the airport's place on the temperature, wind
  and pressure rows; its temperature goes on the terrain-corrected row
  where the panel has one. That row ("TMP 2M · DEM") carries the model's
  2 m temperature to the terrain's height: below the model ground at
  6.5 K/km, above it as the free atmosphere at that height (the run's
  1000–500 hPa temperatures interpolated in their heights) plus the
  model's surface departure faded by `exp(−dz / H)`, H = 2500 m for a
  warm departure and 800 m for a cold one — the REDCAPP
  decomposition (Cao et al. 2017, doi:10.5194/gmd-10-2905-2017) over a
  TopoSCALE free atmosphere (Fiddes & Gruber 2014,
  doi:10.5194/gmd-7-387-2014). With relief on, the map is corrected the
  same way.
- `?radar=<site>` — draw one WSR-88D radar's lowest sweep alone over the
  basemap (`docs/nexrad.md`), the field under it held off screen:
  `?radar=GWX` is Columbus AFB. `?radar=on` only marks the sites over the
  field; a click on one opens it, and re-pressing the pressed product on the
  level row (REF / VEL beside the site and sweep time) goes back to the field.
  `?radarproduct=n0g` shows radial velocity (green toward the radar, red away,
  grey-violet range-folded) instead of reflectivity. The sweep shown is the
  newest at or before the playhead, within 15 minutes, and the level row says
  how far it trails the playhead; past the window the newest is shown faded. It
  follows the playhead and never holds it. Outside a case, over a reflectivity
  (`?type=radar`), every WSR-88D site is marked and an open site reads its
  last three hours live from NOAA's Level 3 bucket, a new sweep within a minute of its arrival. The Rolling
  Fork showcase case (`?case=rolling-fork-2023`) carries DGX, GWX and NQA.
- `?backend=xue` — read each bundle through its `.xue` container where
  the run publishes a Zarr v3 store beside it (the run's shared
  `bundles.zarr/`, the same codes under standard codecs;
  docs/zarr-profile.md). The store is the
  default for every bundle whose manifest entry carries a `zarr`
  descriptor, and the container is what the rest, and every run published
  before stores, play from; the data card reads `Zarr` or `Xue` for the
  path in use. A comparison switch, not shareable state.
- `?x=true` — the experimental synoptic composite: the precipitation on a
  stepped 0.1/1/2/5/10/20/50 mm/h key, the sea level
  pressure lines with their H/L marks over it, the particles run by the
  850 hPa vapour flux, and two fields computed in the browser from several
  bundles, drawn as outlined washes — a warm moist inflow (strong
  `qflux850` in high `thetae850` air) and a frontal zone (a sharp
  `thetae850` gradient). `?x=inflow`, `?x=front` or `?x=none` picks which
  of the two are drawn (the rail's two toggle tiles rewrite it). A look at
  how far the published data goes, not a product; the layers are the
  ordinary ones and `?type=` / `?lines=` still pick them.
- `?model=gibs&gibs=snpp|noaa20|noaa21|terra|aqua` (true colour) or
  `snpp-fc|noaa20-fc|noaa21-fc` (VIIRS M11-I2-I1) or `terra-721|aqua-721`
  (MODIS bands 7-2-1) — NASA GIBS's daily corrected-reflectance picture
  of that platform, a dataset of its own in the model switch, fetched
  from GIBS directly (nothing is published for it): the timeline is the
  last seven UTC days, one picture a day, today's filling in as the
  orbiters pass. The false colour shows burn scars dark red and active
  fires bright.
- Fire fields (no query parameter; a page opens on the published field):
  computed in the browser from published bundles, each a field of its own
  picked on the rail or in the field sheet's fire group, shown only where
  the run ships its inputs. Hotspot: on a geostationary disk, cells whose
  3.9 µm reading is over 310 K by day or 305 K by night with the
  3.9 − 10.4 µm difference over 10 K, standing at least 10 K and four
  standard deviations above the clear cells of the 11 × 11 cells around
  it (or 10 K above them over 320 K by day, 310 K by night), cloud by day
  (10.4 µm at or under 275 K) and sun glint within 12° of the specular
  point left out; needs `ir039` and `ir104`. FFWI: the Fosberg fire
  weather index (0–100) from `tmp2m`, `dpt2m` and `wind10m`. Red flag:
  relative humidity under 30 % with a gust of 10 m/s or more (`tmp2m`,
  `dpt2m`, `gust`). Both over land only where the run ships `soilw1`.
- `#map=<zoom>/<lat>/<lon>` — the view, in the fragment (MapLibre's named
  hash; the page keeps it current on every move). Without it the page opens
  on the dataset's own region: the world for a global model, the contiguous
  United States for `hrrr`, the case's box for a case — or, for a case
  whose catalog row carries a `view`, that camera (center, zoom, pitch,
  bearing, and the relief it asks for unless the link carries
  `?terrain=`).

Examples: `/?model=ecmwf&type=wind850`, `/?type=temp&lines=hgt500`,
`/?case=pnw-heat-dome-2021`, `/?case=ida-2021&type=radar`,
`/?model=hrrr&type=radar#map=6/32.8/-96.8`, `/?type=wind&tc=EP142026`,
`/?type=temp&stations=snd`, `/?model=himawari&type=infrared#map=5/25/140`.

## Data access

Everything the page reads is a plain file with CORS open, under
https://dataset.ringsaturn.me/xue/. The contract is two layers:

- One mutable live pointer per source (JSON, schema 1): `latest.json` (GFS),
  `latest-sflux.json`, `latest-ecmwf.json`, `latest-aifs.json`,
  `latest-ifshres.json`, `latest-hrrr.json`, `latest-gefsaero.json`, `latest-cmadust.json`, `latest-silam.json`, `latest-cfs.json`, `latest-iconeu.json`, `latest-arpege.json`, `latest-mrms.json`, `latest-jma.json`,
  `latest-himawari.json`, `latest-himawarijp.json`, `latest-goeseast.json`,
  `latest-goeswest.json`, `latest-meteosat.json`. Fields: `schemaVersion`,
  `model`, `product`, `run` (YYYYMMDDHH, UTC), `runTime` (ISO 8601),
  `manifestPath` (relative), `manifestCrc32`. Fetch with cache disabled; it
  changes four times a day (every hour for HRRR, every five minutes for
  MRMS — compare `manifestCrc32`, not `run`, to see whether it moved).
- Everything the pointer names is immutable and lives under `<model>.<run>/`:
  the run's `manifest.json` (schema 5: `model`, `product`, `runTime`,
  `forecastHours`, and `bundles[]`, each with `variable`, optional
  half-resolution `variants[]`, a first-frame `poster`, and one or both of two deliveries of the same codes: the `.xue`
  container as `path` + `byteLength` + `crc32` (one unit, present whole or
  absent whole) and a `zarr` store descriptor). A `zarr` descriptor names
  the Zarr v3 store the bundle is in: every bundle of one tier shares one,
  `bundles.zarr/` (`bundles.half.zarr/`, …; runs published earlier have
  `<bundle>.zarr/`), a directory of objects — uint8, one shard per
  variable array holding the whole axis, its inner chunks six-frame time
  chunks of the bundle's tiles, zstd, the bundle's metadata under the
  group's `xue_bundles[<bundle>]` (`docs/zarr-profile.md`) — readable with
  xarray or any Zarr v3 client; its `crc32` is the `?v=` for every object
  in the store, the same on every entry naming it. Every
  live run and every showcase case now ships the store alone; the `.xue`
  container is what runs published before the store carried, and every
  decoder keeps reading it.
  Request an immutable artifact as `<path>?v=<crc32>`. The grid, the time
  axis, the variables' GRIB2 parameter blocks and the quantization codebooks
  are inside each bundle — a UTF-8 JSON metadata block after the container's
  header, the store group's `attributes.xue` verbatim.
- The MRMS and JMA radar windows and the satellite windows are one
  directory deeper: the `run` is the window's *first* hour (three hours
  before the newest frame's, moving on every hour), and each five-minute
  rebuild of that run is a round of its own,
  `mrms.<run>/<HHMM>/manifest.json` (HHMM the round's UTC start), so a
  round's artifacts are never rewritten under a `?v=` a reader may hold.
  A `window.json` beside the manifest (`frameCount`, `firstSlot`,
  `latestSlot`, `hours`, `round`) says which frames the round holds. The
  live run's last two rounds and the previous run's are kept; older rounds
  are deleted once the pointer has moved on.
- The same runs and cases are also described as a static STAC 1.1.0
  catalog derived from the documents above (`docs/stac.md`; nothing here
  replaces them): `catalog.json` at the root, one `<source>/collection.json`
  per live source whose `item` / `latest-version` links name the run the
  pointer names, one `<source>.<run>/item.json` per run beside its
  manifest — an asset per artifact (the store as `application/vnd.zarr`,
  `file:size` / `file:checksum` from the manifest's bytes and CRC, the
  manifest itself under its `?v=`), the grid and axis as `cube:dimensions`,
  every array as `cube:variables`, the cycle as
  `forecast:reference_datetime` — and `showcase/collection.json` with an
  Item per case. The point products below are in it on the same
  terms: `sounding/`, `airport/`, `synop/`, `tc/`, `nexrad/` and `fire/` each carry a `collection.json`
  and the live `item.json`, with one `<product>.<issue>/item.json` beside
  each index naming its files as assets (the `?v=`-addressed index, the
  NDJSON file or one JSON file per storm) and the stations' bounding box as
  its geometry. Links are relative; the mutable documents are served
  no-cache like the pointer.
- The historical catalog is `showcase.json` at the same root (schema 1,
  `generatedAt`, `cases[]`); each case carries `id`, `title` and `summary`
  keyed by language, `model`, `run`, `runTime`, `forecastHours`, `bbox`,
  `variables`, `defaultVariable`, `eventTime`, `tags`, `credit`, and its own
  `manifestPath` + `manifestCrc32`, which resolve like a live run's. An
  optional `view` names the camera the case opens on: `{"center": [lon,
  lat], "zoom": number, "pitch"?: degrees, "bearing"?: degrees,
  "terrain"?: exaggeration | false}`; a row without one is framed on its
  `bbox`, and a `view` the viewer cannot read is ignored, not fatal.
- Tropical cyclones are a separate, hourly JSON product under the same
  root (schema 1, `docs/tc.md`): the mutable pointer `latest-tc.json`
  (`schemaVersion`, `product: "tc"`, `issued`, `path`, `byteLength`,
  `crc32`) names `tc.<YYYYMMDDHH>/index.json`, an immutable directory per
  aggregation hour holding the index (`storms[]` with `id`, `level` A/B/C,
  `basin`, `name`, `path`, `byteLength`, `crc32`, the headline `position`
  / `vmax` / `pmin` / `class`, the keys present; `crosswalk` from retired
  ids; `sources[]` with `ok` and the error when not) and one `<storm
  id>.json` per system: `best` (multi-agency best tracks, IBTrACS keys),
  `agencies` (official forecasts: `nhc`, `jtwc`), `models` (`gfs`, `ecmwf`
  as tracks; `gefs`, `ecmwfens` as member × lead fixed-point arrays, −32768
  missing), `alert` (a JTWC formation alert). A-level ids are ATCF ids
  (`EP142026`); unnumbered systems carry `x-<basin>-<hour>-<n>`. Units
  are SI (m/s, hPa, km, seconds from `base`); wind radii are keyed `34` /
  `50` / `64` (knots, the centres' names) as `[ne, se, sw, nw]` in km.
  Sources: NHC, JTWC, the NCEP GFS/GEFS tracker, ECMWF open data `tf`
  BUFR, IBTrACS. The viewer draws it as tracks over any layer (`?tc=`).
  The storm archive beside it, `tc/archive/catalog.json` (`docs/tc.md` §8–9):
  every distinct forecast of a numbered storm since 2023 by month
  (`<YYYY>/<MM>/forecasts.jsonl` + `index.json` with each storm's byte span),
  each season's best tracks (`<YYYY>/best.jsonl` + `index.json`; IBTrACS'
  history adds earlier seasons of best tracks alone, storms without an ATCF
  number under `WP-<SID>-<season>`) and track errors (`<YYYY>/scores.json`,
  `errors.jsonl`, seasons with forecasts only); every file but the catalog
  is `?v=<crc32>`-addressed and read by Range. Model `gdm` is Google DeepMind's
  experimental track (CC BY 4.0, archived 48 h after its last valid time;
  cite "Contains experimental research data produced by © 2023-25 Google
  LLC ... (CC BY 4.0)").
- Airport observations and forecasts are a separate, ten-minute JSON
  product under the same root (schema 1, `docs/airport.md`): the mutable
  pointer `latest-airport.json` names
  `airport/<YYYY>/<MM>/<DD>/airport.<YYYYMMDDHHMM>/index.json` (the flat
  `airport.<YYYYMMDDHHMM>/index.json` before that layout),
  which carries every station's position and newest observation as a
  compact row (`icao`, `lat`, `lon`, `elev`, `obsTime`, `t`, `td`, `wd`,
  `ws`, `gust`, `vis`, `qnh`, `category`, `tafPresent`, `offset`,
  `length`) and names `history.jsonl` beside it with that file's length
  and CRC32. The history file is one line per station, sorted by ICAO —
  the station with its last 24 hours of METARs and its current TAF — so
  one airport is one range request over the row's `offset` / `length`
  (the span is the JSON object alone and parses by itself) and the whole
  set is one streamed file. Units are SI (°C, m/s, metres, hPa; `vis`
  10000 means ten kilometres or more; `wd` null means a variable
  direction) and the report and the bulletin are kept verbatim in `raw`.
  Source: the NOAA Aviation Weather Center's cache files (public domain),
  the world's services' observations via WMO exchange.

- Radiosonde soundings are a fourth JSON product under the same root,
  hourly (schema 1, `docs/sounding.md`): the mutable pointer
  `latest-sounding.json` names `sounding.<YYYYMMDDHH>/index.json`, an
  immutable directory per aggregation hour holding two files. `index.json`
  carries a per-source `watermark`, `sources[]`, a `soundings` descriptor
  (`path: "soundings.jsonl"`, `byteLength`, `crc32`) and `stations[]` —
  the WIGOS `id`, `wmo`, `lat`, `lon`, `elev`, `latest`, `times`, a
  `headline` of `t500` / `td500` / `freezingLevel` / `pw` / `levels`, and
  the `offset` and `length` of that station's line in `soundings.jsonl`.
  That file is one JSON object per line, sorted by id, each carrying the
  station's newest four nominal times as parallel fixed-point level arrays
  `p` (Pa), `z` (gpm), `t` and `td` (K × 100), `wd` (°), `ws` (m/s × 10)
  and `sig` (BUFR flag table 0 08 042), −32768 missing, plus `n`,
  `reported` (levels before thinning) and `derived` (`freezingLevel`,
  `pw`, `lapse850_500`, `tropopause`). Ascents are thinned to the
  classical TEMP set: every flagged level, the top and bottom, and
  otherwise one level per 3 % of pressure. Read one station
  with `Range: bytes=<offset>-<offset+length-1>` on
  `soundings.jsonl?v=<crc32>` — the span excludes the newline, so it
  parses alone — or stream the whole file for analysis. Sources: the TEMP
  bulletins of the WMO WIS2 Global Cache's two GTS→WIS2 gateways,
  `jp-jma-gts-to-wis2` and `de-dwd-gts-to-wis2` — WMO core data from the
  originating national meteorological and hydrological services. The
  viewer does not read it yet.

- `indicators/` under the data root holds area-weighted weather indicators
  for soybean regions (US Midwest, Brazil, Argentina), computed from the
  published GFS, ECMWF IFS, AIFS and IFS HRES runs: `index.json` (regions,
  features, calendar, files with byte offsets), one append-only
  `features/<source>/<yyyy-mm>.jsonl` per source and month, and
  `season/<region>.<season>.json` running totals. Physical quantities
  only, no market data.

- Surface weather stations are a JSON product under the same root, every
  ten minutes (schema 1, `docs/synop.md`): national observation networks,
  each read by an adapter into one set of elements, JMA AMeDAS (about
  1 300 stations over Japan, ten-minute) the first. The mutable pointer
  `latest-synop.json` names `synop/<YYYY>/<MM>/<DD>/synop.<YYYYMMDDHHMM>/index.json`
  (the flat `synop.<YYYYMMDDHHMM>/index.json` before that layout), which lists
  `networks[]` (id, name, `cadence`, `prPeriod`, the `attribution` to show,
  `license`, `latest`, and its `<network>.jsonl` file with length and
  CRC32), the `elements` order (`t`, `rh`, `p`, `slp`, `wd`, `ws`, `gust`,
  `pr`, `pr1h`, `sun`, `snow`, `vis`) and one compact row per station:
  `id` (`<network>:<number>`, e.g. `amedas:50066` for Mt. Fuji), network
  index, `lat`, `lon`, `elev`, `rank` (0 principal, 1 automatic, 2
  precipitation gauge), `name`, `obsTime`, the current value of each
  element, then the `offset` / `length` of the station's line in its
  network's file. That line holds the last 24 hours as columns: `time`
  (epoch seconds, oldest first) and `obs.<element>` arrays as long, null
  where not reported. Units are SI (°C, %, hPa, m/s, mm, minutes of
  sunshine, cm of snow, metres of visibility); doubtful or missing values
  are null; nothing is derived. AMeDAS is reused under JMA's website terms
  (Public Data License v1.0): credit 「出典：気象庁ホームページ」.

- Air quality is a JSON product under the same root, twice an hour
  (schema 1, `docs/aq.md`): monitoring networks (US EPA AirNow, Hong Kong
  EPD) read into one element table — `pm25`, `pm10` (µg/m³), `o3`, `no2`,
  `so2` (ppb), `co` (ppm), hourly means, nothing derived. The mutable
  pointer `latest-aq.json` names `aq/YYYY/MM/DD/aq.<YYYYMMDDHHMM>/index.json`
  (or the flat `aq.<round>/index.json`), which lists `networks[]` (with
  `preliminary`, the `attribution` to show, `license`) and `elements`;
  each network has a `<network>.stations.json` of compact rows (`id`,
  `lat`, `lon`, `elev`, `rank`, `name`, `agency`, `obsTime`, one current
  value per element, then the `offset` / `length` of the station's line in
  `<network>.jsonl`, its 24-hour window as columns). AirNow data are
  preliminary and their terms forbid publishing a derived index; credit
  each station's `agency`.

- Weather warnings are a JSON product under the same root, every five
  minutes (schema 1, `docs/alerts.md`): every warning US NWS, JMA and ECCC
  have in force, each filed under one of sixteen categories and a common
  level 1–5 (5 is JMA's 特別警報 alone), with the service's own event
  name, code and level kept verbatim. The mutable pointer
  `latest-alerts.json` names `alerts/YYYY/MM/DD/alerts.<round>/index.json`,
  whose `alerts[]` rows are `[id, network, category, level, event, sent,
  onset, expires, west, south, east, north, offset, length]`; each
  network's `<network>.jsonl` holds the full records (texts in every
  language the service publishes, area codes, simplified polygon). Area
  codes resolve against boundary sets under `alerts-areas/` (PMTiles plus a
  `.bbox.json` of every code's box). A monthly archive is under
  `alerts/archive/`.

- Active fires are a JSON product under the same root, every hour (schema
  1, `docs/fire.md`): NASA FIRMS's near-real-time detections from VIIRS
  (S-NPP, NOAA-20, NOAA-21, 375 m) and MODIS (Terra, Aqua, 1 km) over a
  rolling seven days. The mutable pointer `latest-fire.json` names
  `fire.<YYYYMMDDHH00>/index.json`, which carries `window` (`start`,
  `end`), `sensors[]` (id such as `viirs-noaa20`, name, `resolution` in
  metres, the `attribution` to show, `license`, `latest` acquisition,
  `count`, and its `<sensor>.jsonl` file with length and CRC32) and
  `hours[]` rows `[sensor index, hour, count, frpMax MW, offset, length]`,
  sorted by sensor then hour. Each line of a sensor file is one UTC hour:
  `hour` (epoch seconds), `n`, and columns `t` (seconds after the hour),
  `lat` / `lon` (integers of 1e-4°), `frp` (0.1 MW), `bt` (fire-channel
  brightness temperature, 0.1 K), `conf` (one character per detection,
  `l` / `n` / `h`) and `dn` (`D` / `N`). One sensor's hours are back to
  back, so any span of hours is one Range request. FIRMS data are NASA
  open data; acknowledge LANCE FIRMS (NASA ESDIS).

A `.xue` bundle is one gridded variable (or a u/v pair) for a whole run:
8-bit quantized planes on the native grid, temporal residual prediction in
anchor groups, one Zstandard frame per spatial tile per group, all indexed so
a viewport or a single point's time series can be fetched by byte range. The
format is specified in `docs/format.md` (link below). Decoders you can call:

- Python: `pip install xuepy`, then `import xue` — opens a bundle, decodes a
  frame or one cell's whole series to a NumPy array of quantized codes (the
  metadata's codebook dequantizes them), and carries the native encoder.
  https://pypi.org/project/xuepy/
- Rust: crate `xue` on crates.io, API docs at https://ringsaturn.github.io/xue/
- The build pipeline itself (`xuebuild`, in the repository) fetches a run
  from the public NOAA / ECMWF buckets and writes all of the above.

## Documentation

- [README](https://github.com/ringsaturn/xue/blob/main/README.md): what the
  project is, the sources, quick start, using the data, URL parameters,
  licensing.
- [Sources](https://github.com/ringsaturn/xue/blob/main/docs/sources.md):
  what each source publishes, its grid, axis and caveats.
- [Zarr store profile](https://github.com/ringsaturn/xue/blob/main/docs/zarr-profile.md):
  the normative layout of the published stores.
- [Format specification](https://github.com/ringsaturn/xue/blob/main/docs/format.md):
  the normative `.xue` container spec (both container versions, the bundle
  metadata schema, quantization and the residual arithmetic).
- [Native encoder](https://github.com/ringsaturn/xue/blob/main/docs/encoder.md):
  the Rust port of the encoder and how it is held byte-identical to the
  Python reference.
- [Tropical cyclone product](https://github.com/ringsaturn/xue/blob/main/docs/tc.md):
  the normative description of the hourly track product — delivery,
  units, identity rules, the index, storm and pointer files.
- [Airport product](https://github.com/ringsaturn/xue/blob/main/docs/airport.md):
  the normative description of the ten-minute METAR / TAF product —
  delivery, units, identity, and the index, history and pointer files.

- [Surface station product](https://github.com/ringsaturn/xue/blob/main/docs/synop.md):
  the normative description of the ten-minute surface station product —
  delivery, the elements and units, identity, the index, the network files
  and each network's source and terms.
- [Active fire product](https://github.com/ringsaturn/xue/blob/main/docs/fire.md):
  the normative description of the hourly FIRMS fire product — delivery,
  the detection encoding, the sensors, the index, the sensor files and the
  terms.
- [Radiosonde sounding product](https://github.com/ringsaturn/xue/blob/main/docs/sounding.md):
  the normative description of the hourly sounding product — delivery, the
  fixed-point level arrays, station identity, the index, the station file,
  the sources and the derived quantities.
- [STAC catalog](https://github.com/ringsaturn/xue/blob/main/docs/stac.md):
  the catalog / collection / item layout derived beside the manifests, what
  each document carries and where it comes from.
- [Authoring cases](https://github.com/ringsaturn/xue/blob/main/showcase/README.md):
  how a historical event becomes a cropped, permanently published case.

## Optional

- [llms-full.txt](https://xue.ringsaturn.me/llms-full.txt): the user-facing
  documents above in one file, generated at each deploy.
- [Sitemap](https://xue.ringsaturn.me/sitemap.xml): the two pages and every
  published case.
- [Publishing workflows](https://github.com/ringsaturn/xue/tree/main/.github/workflows):
  the scheduled jobs that fetch, encode and upload each source.
